utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. May I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. And now we have to finish your cross-examination by Mr. Lukic. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujic, good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two brief interventions; it's something about yesterday's transcript. On 4759, line 10 and line 11, my question was interpreted somewhat clumsily and I believe Mr. Vujic provided a crystal clear answer. I would just like to repeat that question. My question was: Is the witness familiar with the provisions of the law on criminal procedure which envisaged criminal responsibility for all those giving false testimony. Your answer was recorded. And the second thing is on page 4774, line 17, I asked the witness the following: "After the meeting in Velepromet when he saw Major Lukic," and the transcript says "at the meeting in Velepromet," whereas we know that Major Lukic did not attend that meeting at Velepromet. So I believe this needs to be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujic, we shall now continue with our questions. Can you please keep your answers as brief as possible because I have limited time available to me. I will ask you questions about Negoslavci on the 19th when you arrived at about 2000 hours. Do you remember or do you know that the headquarters of the security body of the Guards Brigade was in the same building as the command operations group south?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on whatever information I had, I know that Major Sljivancanin was the chief of the security body and he was the technical organ, in a manner of speaking, on behalf of the commander. Only he was allowed to go there and everybody else was allowed to come only if they were previously invited by Major Sljivancanin or the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the headquarters. Was it there or not?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please answer yes or no. When you arrived and when the meeting began at Colonel Mrksic's, was Major Sljivancanin there already or did he arrive later on?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me try to distinguish. I am certain that he wasn't there when we greeted each other, everybody who was there, which probably means that he arrived at some point after the introductions were made to Colonel Mrksic, Colonel Pavkovic, and Lieutenant-Colonel Panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's not try to repeat ourselves. Both your groups were there. We know who was there.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will stray from my line of questioning slightly, but it's something I wanted to ask you yesterday. Do you know if such operations groups belonging to the 1st Military District or belonging to the security administration, did such groups go to Operations Group North as well? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I have no information on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You all remained together in that meeting. And after your meeting with Sljivancanin, you all left for Velepromet, I mean your operatives. Right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for the substance of your meeting with Colonel Mrksic and as for what you remember being told at that meeting by both Mrksic and Sljivancanin, this is something you testified at length about, both to the investigating magistrate, to the military court at the Belgrade trial, and here. You agree with me; right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the OTP of The Hague Tribunal, you said you had the impression and you believe that Mr. Sljivancanin was speaking truthfully when he was speaking at that meeting and you believe what he told you?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did you as a colonel accept the fact that a major, a lower-ranking person, was referring to you about these missions and tasks?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was just passing them on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you accepted that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that at the meeting with Colonel Mrksic it was in your presence that Mrksic told Sljivancanin that he should go and talk to the medical chief Jovanovic about those doctors who were supposed to leave the next day?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you personally speak at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Can you please say more about which meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I mean the meeting with Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Slavko Tomic was asking some questions. I'm not sure if it was here at the meeting with Colonel Mrksic, but we looked at a chart representing our losses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All I want to know is whether you personally contributed to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I did, or at least I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you at that point in time or later on when you talked to Sljivancanin say that you had been sent by the security administration to provide technical assistance?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Slavko Tomic as the head of that group was asking questions. That was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now talk about your conversation that evening with Mr. Sljivancanin at Negoslavci, so that's the meeting I'm talking about now. That was the meeting after your conversation with Colonel Mrksic. How long do you think this conversation was, your conversation with Major Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be very accurate. I'm sure you understand. Major Sljivancanin made the schedule and the agenda. He decided what the substance of the meeting would be or the agenda, as any officer would.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that your meeting with Colonel Mrksic lasted about 10 or 15 minutes. In relation to that, was this one shorter or longer?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was shorter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will try to quote your testimony about what my client told you. He told you that Vukovar had been liberated. Please just say whether what I'm suggesting is true.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Vukovar had been liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That the opposite side had surrendered at Mitnica?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't speaking about an opposite side; he was using the kind of language used normally in combat operations. He was saying "Ustashas," "the enemy," and the Croats were using the same kind of expressions, Serbo-Chetniks, Chetniks, enemies, that kind of thing. My apologies for being a bit extensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He did mention this surrender at Mitnica, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said this was the last Croat stronghold, the last area of resistance. He said that there had been talk of conditions for this surrender and that Colonel Pavkovic was there to arrange that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On 4493 of the transcript you said several days ago that he said at the time that many potential criminals of war were hiding in the hospital, fearing surrender, and that they were disguising themselves.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that the situation was unclear at the hospital or that the situation at the hospital was particularly unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just reminding you what you said.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that there were Croatian paramilitaries at Velepromet who were mingling with the civilians.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My testimony was slightly different, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have just read exactly what you -- but if you want me to, I can go back to what you stated. So what do you think you said?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I believe Mr. Sljivancanin have spoken about this in reply to Colonel Tomic's question, having been asked how many captured Ustashas there were. And then Major Sljivancanin said they didn't know the exact number because they were surrendering at different stages and they were mingling with civilians. They were coming with civilians. You couldn't tell who was who there. There were about 2.000 people mingling at Velepromet. There were more civilians there than men of military age, those Ustashas, criminals, and that TO members were mingling with the crowd, too. He also said that Velepromet, the facility of Velepromet, was being secured by a military police unit, a unit that was either subordinate to him or to Colonel Mrksic. And this unit was being led by such and such officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He told you that the buses would be there that evening that were supposed to ...

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We must have made some questions to him about things that we weren't sure about. We didn't know what the plan was about, so obviously there was some degree of uncertainty in terms of our role as officers or military people. We didn't know what the plan was. He told us not to worry because there were no special surprises in store for us, he said. Everything had been planned and arranged. The buses would be there. It was all well-rehearsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll go back to some statements that we were using yesterday. I suppose you gave back your copies?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please have a look. Can you please look at the statement you gave to the military court.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there's something you want to challenge, please just ask away. I don't think I even need to look at these statements. These are my statements. Just ask a question, I'll answer as best I can. You don't need to remind me that I said one thing there and another thing here. We are now here in order to shed light on everything that happened, so please if you could just ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is with the Court's help that I'm asking you questions. So it's up to the Chamber to decide if my questions are allowed or not. I have placed documents before you because that is an established practice here.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of my learned friend from the OTP the English copy, we're talking about page 8 and 9, the last passage. And, Witness, please, could you go to page 7?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of my first statement?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters didn't hear what counsel said in reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the B/C/S copy -- English 4 and the B/C/S is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the page of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 4 -- my apologies to the interpreters. The English is page 4, paragraph 2. "After that, Sljivancanin informed us that the last stronghold and the last points of resistance in Vukovar had been broken, that soldiers and civilians had already been surrendering en masse, that a provisional collection centre was set up near the Velepromet company which was near the barracks. There were around 2.000 people there, many of which women, children, old people, and other civilians. It was impossible to know which of them had been involved in the armed rebellion or may have committed crimes. Furthermore, he said that it was necessary to separate the men between 16 and 65 years of age from the women. He also said that that same night as soon as the buses were there, the men must board the buses, be taken to the collection centre at Sremska Mitrovica, and that these persons would then continue to be processed there." We'll go to something else now and then I'll ask you the question. Your statement to the OTP, if you could have a look, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of my learned friend the page number is 8, the bottom of page 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, it's page 7 for you. The last sentence. This is you testifying about that same fact. "He said that our task would be as soon as the military buses were there to separate the prisoners of war from the women and children at Velepromet. He made a special reference to men between 16 and 65 years of age. These were to be put on buses, after which they were to be evacuated to Sremska Mitrovica, as planned. He said the buses would be arriving during the night." Let us now please have a look at what you said in relation to this same topic while testifying at the Belgrade trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of my learned friend page 9 in English, page 33 of your testimony in the Ovcara case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the same topic. I'm reading the bottom of page 33. "Our task would be to coordinate the separation, the separation of men aged between 16 and 65 from the women and children, that the buses would be arriving at around 2200 or 2300 hours, and that the situation was such that there was no need for us to worry, the situation was under control, and the officers of the military police unit were securing the area. They were good at their job, and all that we had to do was wait for the buses." Did you say all that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said all of these things to different investigators, and I was talking about the same subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And essentially ...

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Essentially on the same topic and the substance of my statement is the same and my words are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question to you now is: Why is it that you said something before this Chamber for the very first time; it is something that you didn't even share with the Prosecutor while you were being proofed, namely, you testified here that Sljivancanin had then told you that the triage had already been completed. You said that here for the very first time?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that in front of me, but not only in front of me, he said that in front of everybody.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did you give a completely different story three times?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three completely different questions put by three different court representatives or judges. Everybody phrased their questions in different terms and attempted to see whether I was concealing something, misrepresenting something, whether something was not clear. They all wanted to clarify what it was that we had been given as a task. I said in front of this Trial Chamber quite frankly how it was in response to your questions. I described the sequence of events.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when testifying before the military court and before -- and when testifying before the Belgrade court where you testified as a witness and in front of the investigative judge Alimpic, where you testified as a witness, you kept quiet about this fact?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic, I didn't keep quiet about anything. I wish I would want to know what Mr. Sljivancanin said, what he did there, and Thursday, the 2nd day of March, what he conveyed to me, but I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us proceed. In view of the assignment you received back from your superiors at the security administration, the one that we mention yesterday, in view of how you imagined the reason of your arrival in Vukovar, why would you, as a senior officer within the security administration, be dispatched to board the buses and not do what you had come there to do?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this is why we came there. That was the most complex issue in the history of wars, at least as far as I studied them, how to separate prisoners of war from civilians and how to protect their lives and take them to a location where they would be safe and where certain procedural steps can be taken, as prescribed by the international laws of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely, knowing what could potentially happen there, the generals in charge who were responsible for implementation of the laws had sent three colonels there to ensure that the task would be carried out appropriately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujic, whenever you gave statements, you were given an opportunity to correct anything you had stated previously. This was so in 2000 when you gave testimony to The Hague investigators and this was so when you spoke to Mr. Moore several days ago, but you never made this correction.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what stated just now before you and before Mr. Sljivancanin is, in fact, a correction. Prior to that, both when I testified before the special court and before the investigative court, Major Sljivancanin was not present. I am now saying this in his presence about what I heard and what he said, and he can confirm to you whether this is true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will give you the position of my client straight away. He is claiming that he did not state this, but rather stated what you had said previously in your prior statements.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not how it is. There are other witnesses who can confirm what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Immediately thereafter, after the meeting with Sljivancanin, you went to Velepromet. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Never in the past, never until Thursday last week when you started testifying before this Trial Chamber and also in your proofing with the OTP, you never, ever stated that Sljivancanin held a meeting with you in front of the command on the road. You stated this for the first time here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't quite say that it was on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, it was in front of the building?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In front of the building where the headquarters was housed?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, where the headquarters was housed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you made corrections of your statement at a meeting held with the OTP on the 14th of February, you signed this statement, this corrigendum. Item 1 was read out to Mr. Moore, item one of the addendum, and it says: "The meeting with Mr. Sljivancanin at the command headquarters in Negoslavci," and so on. Once again you stated "at the command headquarters."

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, a part of the meeting was held inside the command headquarters with Mr. Sljivancanin, and then a part was held in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us conclude --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The substance was the same. We discussed the same assignment. He informed us -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was waiting for the interpretation. So the meeting with Sljivancanin continued, and from the building you went out into the street?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not literally into the street. That's not how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The position of my client is as follows: At that time, as you were about to depart for Velepromet, you expressed a wish to go to the hospital on the following day?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The hospital was discussed on that occasion because Colonel Slavko Tomic asked whether that evening the hospital would be evacuated as well. Major Sljivancanin said that it wouldn't until the situation was assessed at the hospital and that it would be done only on the following day in the morning and that a decision would be taken as to who would go there, but that that was a different plan and that he personally would be in charge of that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now turn to another topic regarding the same event. Please take a look at your statement given to the military court. Based on what I can see - and you will probably agree with me - half a page pertains to what you heard on that occasion from Mrksic and Sljivancanin. This is densely typed text of your statement. We didn't hear your answer. Would you please give an audible answer. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your statement given to the OTP investigators after four days of interview, one and a half page of densely typed text pertains to what you remembered and conveyed about that conversation. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you gave your first statement to The Hague investigators, you provided one correction in relation to your military court statement, and this is what Investigative Judge Trifunovic wrote about how he interpreted what you said about hearing sounds near Ovcara, and you said that it was misinterpreted. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please give me a yes or no answer and then we'll proceed further. Never in front of any judge or investigative judge or in front of the OTP investigators did you state a sentence that you said for the first time here and the same sentence you said two days prior to that to my colleague Mr. Moore. The sentence on page 4497 about how Sljivancanin, as you were leaving added to you: Don't be surprised if you see a Chetnik slaughter an Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't be surprised if Chetniks start slaughtering there. Is that how it was written?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. But Ustashas were also mentioned.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said, "if Chetniks start slaughtering there." Mr. Lukic, was this written down as I said? There was also comment by warrant officer Korica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's in there.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to repeat it. He said: It will be interesting if --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did he say. Will you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be interesting to see how Chetniks hold a public demonstrate on slaughtering or slitting throats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You repeated this but you didn't answer my question. My question was different. We didn't want to hear this once again; we wanted you to state before this Trial Chamber that this is something that you had never stated before any other court.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I didn't say this in front of any other court or any other institution to which I gave a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that this is a memorable sentence. One doesn't forget easily such a question. This is a sentence that definitely causes goose bumps?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, especially in my case because I thought about this subsequently and I also had that encounter with Vojvoda that I described to you, where he, Vojvoda, a leader of a unit of Chetniks held a knife to my throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you remembered this sentence only once you came to see Mr. Moore?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I carried this sentence with me for a long time, for 14 years, and I'm happy to be able to express my sentiments here before this Trial Chamber and also to preserve them, but also to put my thoughts into balance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, that day when you went to Velepromet to a meeting with Borisavljevic, with your colleagues, Korica was there, did you comment on this sentence about what you had heard from Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, it was inappropriate to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will now read page 7. Page 7 of your statement to The Hague investigators, English version page 9. Once again this has to do with the conversation with Sljivancanin. This is how you described it to the OTP. You said: "He also mentioned that several members of the staff unit of the Serbian TO of Vukovar were in Velepromet; however, he didn't give us any details about those units."

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What is in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Nothing. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is in dispute in relation to my prior statements or in relation to what I'm saying here now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This sentence that you uttered to The Hague investigators, you are now denying it?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not disputing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're not disputing it. All right. Let us now take your sentence given to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear which statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- when you came -- your statement given to the military court, page 7, penultimate paragraph, second sentence. You're describing what you said to Mrksic upon your arrival. "On that occasion I was upset because we were not informed of the actual problems in relation to the behaviour of members of Territorial Defence and volunteers, and thus we did not have a plan in advance about how to act in such a situation."

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see anything that should be disputed here either, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. So you took it against Mrksic, the fact that you had not been warned, and in relation to Sljivancanin you had a different attitude?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you saw how the events unfolded and how problems erupted. The judge of the military court interviewed me about the circumstances under which the crime was committed. He already interviewed me -- or rather, we don't know whether he interviewed me about the circumstances under which persons committed crimes or about circumstances relating to my presence there and my description of events and facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Why did you then tell him at length what you told him and The Hague investigators without telling him this sentence?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what the judge asked me. The investigators followed a somewhat different methodology in interviewing then, and my answers were adapted to their questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that my learned friend Mr. Moore has a special methodology, to remind you.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I came to this court to set straight everything I had stated so far. You can see how many documents there are here, how many pages, quite a paperwork.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us proceed. Did you ask my client to take certain steps in relation to events? Did you do this in accordance with your authorities?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please say the name. Don't say "client." I have a lot of respect for Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Upon your return from Velepromet, did you ask Mr. Sljivancanin to take certain measures?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I? That was his unit. He had sent me to a facility over which he had responsibility. Major Sljivancanin had responsibility over that facility; he was responsible to Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will get to that later. Let us now turn back to your statement given to the Belgrade court, page 34. We're still dealing with the same topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Moore, in the English version this is page 10.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, which page did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 34, middle of the page. "During the meeting, while the assignments were issued" -- this is now referring to the meeting with Borisavljevic --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And with other commanding officers. Borisavljevic was not the most senior. Colonel Tomic, was both in terms of his age and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, let me finish my quotation. "During the meeting while assignments were being issued, I noticed that some heads were popping through the door lead being into the room, the heads of bearded, unkempt men. And I asked: "Who are these people?" Up until that time I didn't know that there was a unit there called the Chetniks, and I did not envisage nor did I hear that there were any assessments indicating that we could expect something unpleasant from them. That was probably quite a surprise for me."

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I said. That's precisely what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With you that accurate what you said?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see what you're challenging, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your testimony here you said that the transcript from the Belgrade trial was your most reliable statement. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would include this testimony, too, Mr. Lukic, because the accused are present.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I've just read out to you, you testified under oath as a witness. This is diametrically opposed to your testimony before this Trial Chamber, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Let's move on to Velepromet. Your departure for Velepromet, on that day did you know that on that same day in the morning, just before 1200 hours before you came, Cyrus Vance was there with some high-ranking company. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that in the media, and I realised that he was being escorted by a number of officers, specifically I saw Colonel Nebojsa Pavkovic, but I didn't know that he toured Velepromet and I didn't know what was there or what he saw there. He could have seen something else and I could have seen something else. And what I saw is what I have described here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you about how it looks from the perspective of my client, Mr. Sljivancanin. You as a security officer, would you allow a high-level delegation to enter a facility where there was real danger to their security?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am telling you again that what I came across there was not necessarily the same thing as they did. And what I experienced may not have necessarily been the same thing as Mr. Cyrus Vance had been shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are a security officer. You are in charge of an area, say. Your commander is on his way, for example.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there's no need for this. I know full well who Cyrus Vance is; I know why he was there. I know why he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation. There is no problem, Mr. Vujic. We're both creating an enormous amount of difficulty for the transcript. It will be very difficult to decipher later on. Thank you. Let's move on to something else, and then perhaps we may at one point go back to this. I'll ask you several questions about Srecko Borisavljevic. There's one point where I agree with you. I have to hand it to you. Mr. Srecko Borisavljevic was subordinated to Mr. Sljivancanin in the security chain of command. He was a captain first class with a security unit of the guards brigade.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police chain of command, too, that applies as well, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, sir, please. I am putting it to you that he was not a military police officer, that he only became -- that there was a military police officer at Velepromet called Nenad Bajic and that Srecko Borisavljevic was a officer -- a military police officer at the barracks, which also covered Velepromet. Would I be wrong in saying that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you wouldn't be wrong, but I'll be very honest with this Chamber, brutally honest. Nenad Bajic is my neighbour. My house is 74 and his house is 82. If I go back to my old neighbourhood, I am likely to say hi to his father. I knew Nenad Bajic. I saw him there. But I have to tell you this: The person in command there was captain First Class Srecko Borisavljevic. Who was his superior? Well, Major Sljivancanin, Colonel Mrksic know that, don't they.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, who?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I say?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Srecko Borisavljevic was ordered by my client, Mr. Sljivancanin, to meet you there?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me he was the person reporting to me and Mr. Lukic in any army. You know full well what that means, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honour, I am trying to keep the situation under control, but I do believe it might be appropriate to draw the witness's attention to some procedural facts. I am really trying to focus on my questions. I'm not trying to create a source of tension, and I don't think the witness should either.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, really, but you are taunting me. That's a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you would bear in mind, please, Mr. Vujic, that the process here is for counsel to ask questions, not for the judges, which is not a process that you may be readily familiar with so that when counsel for each interested party, Prosecution and each accused, asks questions, that is the way that we learn of the events. If a counsel is asking you matters that you find you don't agree with, you say so. If you find he's putting to you matters that you find objectionable, you can say so. But don't think that the counsel is trying to do that just to upset you or antagonise you. It is his job and his responsibility to put those matters to you so that you can comment on them so that we will know your position about that matter. So please try and answer as calmly as you can so as to indicate whether you agree with what is put to you or disagree with it. And if you disagree, indicate where you disagree.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vujic, let's try to go through this briefly, if we can. If there's anything you need to add, I'm sure Mr. Moore will be re-examining you. Yesterday you confirmed to me what you had stated to The Hague Prosecutor when I asked you about the hospital evacuation. You said that Major Sljivancanin was in charge of the evacuation and that it was under the command of the military police officer who was there, and you met him. That's what you said yesterday. Today my question is -- my question to you as an expert: A security body can only be in technical control of the military police but only an officer can command a military police unit. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation of Major Sljivancanin's role was as follows. He was both the security body present there and he was the commander of the military police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm putting it to you that he was never the commander. There are two military police battalions and two military police battalion commanders, but you didn't know about this so we may as well move on.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Major Gavalic was one of the commanders and he was nowhere to be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was replaced by Major Susic, but -- well, no matter.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is: Major Sljivancanin was in control of the hospital's evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to Velepromet, please. You say Srecko Borisavljevic reported to you upon your arrival. You surveyed the scene and you were off to that meeting. That's your testimony. Right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the OTP you suggest that the meeting went on from 2300 hours to 2330. You said that to Mr. Vasic and you said that before the military court. Right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I don't think it's really that material, when exactly the meeting was held. I think the substance of that meeting and what was actually said is what matters. What does matter is that the meeting was held before any steps were taken, before any missions were carried out, and before the buses arrived. The assignments were set out at the meeting. I believe I was crystal clear about that particular aspect in all of my statements, except that with my statement before the military court, the investigating magistrate turns things around somehow or twisted the time-line of these events, that the meeting was held later, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please correct me if I'm wrong. I'm asking you about the time-line. I believe it is important. You are shifting the times, as it were, in order to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the last part of counsel's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, by no means, Mr. Lukic. I was thinking that you were trying to clarify the exact time-line of events there and not necessarily what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please be asked to speak one at a time in order to ensure accurate interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was not recorded. My theory was: You are shifting the times or the time-line, as it were, in order to justify the discrepancy in your testimony before the military court where you said that first you visited the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Again the interpreter didn't hear the last part of counsel's question. Please speak one at a time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vujic, you are jumping in even before Mr. Lukic finishes his question. The interpreter is about half a sentence behind you - he has to be - so that he cannot finish what Mr. Lukic says and hear what you say, and that is a constant pattern. So if you'd please try and hold your tongue for that little bit longer until Mr. Lukic is finished and the interpreter can finish, and then if you can give your answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Count to five; that's what I should be doing too, I suppose. I'll go back to this a little later. My next question. Do you remember the conversation you had with Sljivancanin at Negoslavci, the first meeting? Do you remember Sljivancanin telling you that the Territorial Defence staff of Vukovar was in charge of Velepromet or in control and they were there? Do you remember him telling you that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does the name of Ljubinko Stojanovic mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting my learned friend. It's really the way he has phrased the question that causes me a little concern. "Do you remember Sljivancanin telling you that the Territorial Defence staff." If my learned friend is going to be saying that this was what was actually said by Sljivancanin, then it should be put to him in clearer terms so he has a chance to say: Well, that occurred or not, and not couching it in a way that suggests in actual fact it is right when it has never been said. If that's the way the challenge is going to be put, it's got to be clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is that your instructions about an aspect of what was said by your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you could allow the witness to comment directly on that, rather than: Do you remember, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tried to tell the witness exactly what my client told me he said at the time, his very words. I quoted what my client remembers when he spoke to me about it, and that's what my question is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujic, did Sljivancanin on that occasion mention the fact that Velepromet was in control of Vukovar's TO, and that their headquarters was there, too?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can answer the question now.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was all mixed up there, civilians, POWs, TO people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about Zigic Nenad, does that name mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The meeting at Velepromet where you attended with your officers, the people from the military police and Borisavljevic, at that meeting was there anyone from Vukovar's TO Staff? Did anybody introduce themselves as members of the TO Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one like that was ever introduced to me at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your statement before the military court, page 5, page 5 in English as well, halfway down the page. "Also at the meeting where representatives -- or rather, officers from the TO unit and the volunteers who had been invited." Did you state that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain. If somebody's asking you trick questions: Were there representatives of the TO present at that meeting, for example, and I said yes. What if I had said: No, there were no such people there. And then later I go on to explain how heads were popping in and out of that door, bearded faces, people wearing different kind of uniform but not the JNA uniform, well that sort of answers your question, doesn't it? And if I'm not answering your question, again, the question would be: How am I supposed to answer the question. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's move on. On the 16th of February -- just a minute, please. I think this was on the 16th of February. The page is 73 of the draft transcript. I don't have the official page yet, unfortunately, but I'm sure you will remember. You had begun evacuating that room and you called out: "Where is Srecko Borisavljevic?" He was nowhere to be seen. So you told Sekic to send over an officer to Mrksic so Mrksic could send in reinforcements. Isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said and that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please try to remember, did you perhaps tell Borisavljevic to go to Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, Mr. Lukic. Borisavljevic went away from there, just like Colonel Tomic did. In my statements and in my evidence, I used the term "treason." I said that they had betrayed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we heard that. Please take the transcript from the Belgrade trial, page 37.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For my learned friend it's page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm reading the first paragraph, middle of that paragraph. "I ordered Captain Srecko Borisavljevic to go to Colonel Mrksic for help and to ensure that a reinforce arrived arrives in the form of the military police unit so that we can be sure to accomplish our mission."

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said before the special court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under oath?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you testified here under oath as well?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to clarify anything, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. My learned friend Prosecutor is here and you will probably have to do a lot of explaining to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the Tribunal will want to clarify the matter, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vujic, you have said apparently you agree on oath before the court in Belgrade that you ordered the captain to go to Colonel Mrksic for help. I understood your testimony here when you gave it and what you have said a few minutes ago here to be that you did not order the captain to go to Colonel Mrksic for help; he had deserted you. You had ordered someone else. Could you please clarify whether you ordered the captain or someone else or no one to go to Colonel Mrksic for help.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Parker, I stand by this statement I gave just now and also previously, in the previous days, when I described how I acted and how I issued this order. This means that first I called out twice, loudly, Captain Borisavljevic's name. I asked him to respond so that I could issue an order to him to go to Colonel Mrksic, to explain the situation, and to ask for reinforcements in the form of a military police unit. At the Belgrade court when asked by the judge to describe how I acted, I explained, saying that I called out the name, that is to say, ordered Captain Borisavljevic. But there, in front of the special court, in front the chamber and in front of defence counsel and family members, I didn't say anything further in order to spare myself and the public further anguish. The truth is something that I stated before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do I correctly understand your evidence to be that you allowed it to be the impression in the Belgrade court that it was the captain you had ordered to go to Colonel Mrksic for help?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't say that with any bad intentions. I didn't say in front of the Belgrade chamber that the members of my team and operations group had left me, Colonel Slavko Tomic and Colonel Kijanovic. It was very difficult for me to utter that in front of the Belgrade chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I take it your answer is yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. I answered saying that I acted in the way that I described before this Trial Chamber. Over there it was difficult for me to say that Captain Borisavljevic was not there, that he had left the location, abandoned the mission. It was also very difficult for me to say that my superior, Slavko Tomic, had abandoned the mission as well, as well as Colonel Kijanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understand your answer to my original question to be yes, that you allowed the record in Belgrade to appear to be that you had ordered the captain to go to Colonel Mrksic for help? You've explained your reasons, but that's what occurred. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We stated so previously. In relation to your first statement given before the military court, you made corrections concerning the time-line of the events in Velepromet and said that things basically transpired in the way you described them here before this Trial Chamber. If you arrived in Negoslavci at 8.00 - and this is quite reliable information because this is written down in the log-book of the guards brigade - if the meeting with Mrksic lasted for 15 minutes, if the meeting with Sljivancanin lasted also for 15 minutes, if you needed -- first you said 45 minutes to get to Velepromet, even one hour, if based on that you arrived at Velepromet, say, at 10.00, what did you do there for an hour if you scheduled the meeting immediately, if you called the meeting immediately?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand you. What are you challenging? Which time reference are you challenging?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I'm challenging is that you have an extra hour. You say that you arrived at Velepromet at 10.00 and the meeting started at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic. You're not right when claiming so. I'm saying that we were at Velepromet throughout the whole time until the buses arrived. Now, let us see how much elapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no. My question related to the beginning of the meeting in relation to the moment of your arrival. I am putting to you that you arrived at 10.00 and that the meeting started at 11.00, and that in the meantime you toured the facility. So I'm putting to you that the event transpired the way you described it before the military court and which you denied later. This is what I am suggesting to you.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic. This is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now read out to you page 5 of the transcript of the military court, which is something that you're denying. This Trial Chamber needs to be aware of something that you're now denying and that you previously stated before the military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For my learned friends, page 6 of the English version, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "In the meantime the buses arrived in front of Velepromet, accompanied by a military police unit. At that moment, I called for a meeting or scheduled a meeting of all officers who were at the collection centre at Velepromet in order to agree on how to implement this assignment." I know your position; however, the logic of your testimony here does not imply that this is an error. We have a sequence of events: Buses, scheduling of a meeting.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic. I'm telling you that the sequence of events and the implementation of the assignment depended on the arrival of buses. So it needs to be established. Mr. Mrksic and Sljivancanin need to say exactly when the buses arrived. Somebody had to escort, accompany, the buses. The buses had to have some officers on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You remain by your previous statement. We will move on. Give me a brief answer, please. After the buses departed, you remained until the very end, until the last bus departed, and then you returned to Negoslavci. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You claimed here before and repeated just now, you said that you did not want to say so in front of the Belgrade court that your colleagues, Tomic and Kijanovic, basically left you out to hang dry. And on page 7 of your testimony before the military court, you stated this and never denied it in front of any institution. You uttered the following sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For my learned friend English version page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "I did not leave with the column, but rather remained together with all other officers within the Velepromet compound."

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What statement is it, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Trifunovic, military court. It is true that you didn't say that they left, or perhaps you insisted for this to be recorded.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't insist; that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. What would you say if I put it to you that here before this court we listened to the testimony of victims, persons from Velepromet who had been taken away that night, who said that they left Velepromet at around 4.00 a.m.; were they wrong in stating that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Left Velepromet, perhaps. Yes, if somebody hid them and then took them out later on. Also, I didn't know about these victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now proceed to your arrival in Negoslavci. You stated that Sljivancanin was in front of the command headquarters in Negoslavci upon your return from Velepromet. This is where you found him. You said that Tomic was there. You also mentioned Kijanovic. The other colleagues who were with you, Stosic, Muncan, Korica, did they also return there to the command headquarter?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you know, but the position of my client is that on that evening he had a lot of major activities. He interviewed Vesna Bosanac, met with Marin Vidic, met with Aleksandar Vasiljevic, he went to Ovcara to see the refugees who had spent the night there, and his position is that you never saw each other that evening again. This is what he's claiming.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. I just wanted to give you his position. When giving evidence here you said that on page 4522 you told General Jerko Crmaric what you had experienced at Velepromet. The Prosecutor put a question to you at transcript page 4523, asking you whether you informed General Crmaric about the murders. And you stated unequivocally to Mr. Moore that at the time you did not have that information. This is what you stated and what was recorded here in this courtroom. My question is: Did you mention to my client, if you indeed saw him then at 1.00 a.m., did you mention to him all the clashes you had had and did you mention all the murders to him, to Mr. Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, upon my return to the command headquarters, there were a number of officers there, as I said. They were coming and going out and observing, just like I did. Major Sljivancanin was there as well. I accept that he was busy completing all these tasks that you mentioned, but he also went to see Colonel Mrksic to brief him on the results achieved in implementation of tasks. Major Sljivancanin held a meeting with us in relation to the accomplishments with the lists at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, you explained that.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he briefed us on that. He told us how the hospital would be evacuated on the following morning, saying that not all of us could accompany him, but also adding that we would have a meeting in relation to that at 6.00 the following morning at the gate of Velepromet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will now put to you the position of my client. Everything you have stated so far is something that he told you at 8.00 p.m. -- or rather, when you met first time. And then I will give you his second position, that in the morning at the Velepromet gate it was only you and Korica who showed up and not other colleagues. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right, Mr. Lukic, and I have to give you a brief explanation, which means that at 8.00 p.m. Major Sljivancanin did not yet have the lists. He only received them in the course of the night from Mrs. Vesna Bosanac and probably Gjuro Njavro and Marin Vidic. So when it comes to the persons at the hospital, medical staff, doctors, whoever was suspected of crimes, all those people in disguise, he only learned about them when he started collecting information, that is to say in the course of his activities when he started collecting information from Mrs. Bosanac and so on. He held a meeting with us, as I said to you, and informed us briefly about that. And then he said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we know what he said. This is your position. All right. I gave you our position. There will be other witnesses, and it will be duly assessed. Now my next question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, there was a second-limb proposition about the following morning, which the witness hasn't been reminded of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. This is my problem: I am under pressure, too, here looking at the clock. I am aware of your deadline, the one you imposed, and I am trying to do my best to abide by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, you didn't tell us about this other position that I put to you, that at 6.00 in the morning in front of the Velepromet gate it was only you and Korica who showed up to go to the hospital and not other officers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not right, Mr. Lukic. Both groups were there, headed by Colonel Slavko Tomic and all those subordinated to him. Also headed by Major Muncan and those subordinated to him, as well as the group of Major Sljivancanin, his subordinate commanders and his driver as far as I could see. His driver was an officer, too. All of us assembled there at 6.00 a.m. on the 20th of November at the Velepromet gate within the compound, inside the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My learned friend from the Prosecution put a question to you about your travel from Velepromet to the hospital on that morning. I will now put another question to you linked to this issue that Mr. Moore brought up with you. Do you remember at the meeting with Mrksic on the evening of the 20th, did any of the soldiers or officers come to inform about an incident which had happened with soldiers in a vehicle? This is somewhat of a leading question. Let's see if it can be even more leading. Do you remember someone saying in your presence to Mrksic that four soldiers got killed in a tank that evening?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that moment. During the briefing that we received from Colonel Mrksic, towards the end of that briefing a junior officer came, perhaps lance-corporal or a sergeant, and said that a vehicle ran into a mine and that four soldiers were killed. Colonel Mrksic listened to this and then said to the soldier or the non-commissioned officer who arrived to send a cable to the operations centre. And he said that the data should be entered into the chart, the data on the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have this information to where were these soldiers killed who were driving in that APC, the location?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in no position to find out about that, so I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's try to wrap this up. You meet Kijanovic at Negoslavci yet again, and he tells you that he managed to get four JNA soldiers off that bus?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to get them off.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you where specifically? Was it from the hangar at Ovcara? More specifically, did Kijanovic tell you that he and Tomic were in the hangar at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kijanovic said that the buses were at Ovcara when he took those soldiers off. He and Tomic never really parted ways, so I suppose they were there together, too. He also said that those were soldiers who were at the hospital, the room that I described, when I came to that room and what I found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were waiting for the column to set out in Negoslavci that evening, did Kijanovic or Tomic tell you that they entered the hangar at Ovcara where the detainees were?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please go into private session briefly. I'm not sure if there are protective measures involved in any way in relation to the questions that I'm about to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were I to tell you that these persons were not JNA soldiers but rather JNA deserters who had joined the ZNG forces and they introduced themselves to Kijanovic's JNA soldiers at one point --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, please, Mr. Lukic, don't even try to go there. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have ten minutes left, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, there are records of interviews of those soldiers. Colonel Kijanovic took those and they must be in the files of the Vukovar case and the penitentiary facility at Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have exactly ten minutes left. I hope that in view of the time I stole yesterday, I don't think that I will be blamed for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want us to smile benevolently on you, Mr. Lukic. We adjourn now and resume at five past 4.00 and you can have seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujic, I have a couple of questions left for you. I would like to take you back to that moment. You are in the car at Negoslavci with Tomic, Kijanovic, Stosic, and Mirkovic. You can hear something that leaves you with a feeling of anxiety, something that leads you to believe that there's something bad going on. Did you perhaps think of suggesting to your colleagues that perhaps you should drive over to Ovcara to see what was going on? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, that was the longest day in my entire life. There will be no other day like it. For me, that day had 27 hours, not 24. Do you think that this is what I should have done, go there and see if there was anything going on? How do you think I would have been able to get there in the first place?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you or any of your colleagues propose that you go and find General Crmaric or Gvero or Pavkovic, anybody at all from the SSNO who was there or perhaps to go and look for somebody from the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the only place I could have gone is to see Colonel Mrksic, and even that wasn't certain. It wasn't certain that he would have agreed to see me. Slavko Tomic said that he did go to see him about this once the vehicles were in the barracks. He went three times; that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we know that. What about your group leader, Tomic, did he tell you that the mission had been accomplished and were you given approval to leave the area?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that the assignment at Velepromet had been completed. I was angry and I was saying things like there are dead bodies over there --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 20th --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing about any mission being completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What's -- what are your relations with Bogoljub Kijanovic like?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen him for years, for years.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you believe him to be an honourable man?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he was saying something that isn't true, if he was saying something against me, then probably that would define him as a rather dishonourable man.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what about Branko Korica, is he an honourable man?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was guarding my life, and he lived the same experience that I did, or nearly. I can say that he was safe-guarding my safety, my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if perhaps you rubbed either of these people the wrong way, in a manner of speaking, at any time?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so, unless someone put them under pressure. At the end of my testimony, I will tell the Chamber exactly who tried to put pressure on me to not tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I told you that Branko Korica never heard these words about Chetniks and Ustashas, the ones that you talked about before the Trial Chamber, do you think he would be right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think how he could have gotten to Branko Korica without going through the official channels, which leads me to conclude that you must have applied some pressure on Branko Korica in order to get to him in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What if I told you that he said that the two of you were involved in the triage at the hospital together, that he was with you when he found those grenades under one of the beds, that some TO members were with you who then left or who you were abandoned by. He took about 40 persons out of the hospital, none of them wounded, all civilians, and took these persons to the buses. What would you say about that?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he carried out that assignment. I find that unlikely because he spent most of the time with me outside in the courtyard. It's true that he left me a number of times to go and see what the others were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujic, you were on an official mission in Vukovar on the 19th and the 20th. You were insulted. You were attacked. You were verbally abused. You were even threatened with assassination. You were attacked by Topola. You were told about a sniper who had his mind set on shooting you. You began to have suspicions, silent ones, at least, that something really dreadful was happening at Ovcara. The only thing you actually asked at Sid was the following sentence: Do you know what's going on? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. General Babic, we're on first-name terms. Mile Babic, do you know what's going on over there? Ljubisa, I didn't even say "Petkovic," do you know what's going on? Do you know what happened there? And they invariably said: Yes, we do, we are aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My last question or second-last question: Do you believe that you acted in keeping with the rules when you told Babic and Petkovic and invoked late Colonel Tomic about this when you asked them: Do you know what's going on there? Do you think that you acted in keeping with the regulations?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I hear of General Babic having passed away. You called him a colonel, and this is the first I hear of it. I wasn't aware of the fact that he passed away. I know how Colonel Petkovic was killed, and I attended his funeral. He is no more. I attended Slavko Tomic's funeral, too; he is no more. But there are other persons, other witnesses, who are still alive. Likewise, the prosecutor is gone who monitored the work of our security bodies, who supervised our work, who gave us our assignments. He's now gone. He committed suicide. I was expecting you to mention his name, too, but you didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I only mentioned the names of those --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You failed to mention the prosecutor. You know what a prosecutor is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is: Do you believe you acted in keeping with the regulations when you asked them that, when you said that sentence, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my moral integrity is concerned, as far as my sense of duty is concerned, I made the greatest possible contribution to attaining truth before this Trial Chamber, before the Defence counsel present here, and before the accused. Please go ahead and verify all of my statements, but do it in an honourable way and do it responsibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not interrupting you. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My testimony is liable to verification, no doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In answer to the questions of my learned friends you felt offended a number of times; I don't believe it was anybody's intention. One thing today's testimony seems to imply is, by way of a conclusion - please tell me if I'm wrong - you say that your account before this Honourable Trial Chamber is your final account. What about the Belgrade military court? What about the Belgrade special court, are those institutions less honourable then in comparison?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic, I have great respect for the president of the chamber of the special court in Belgrade. He guided he. He encouraged me to tell the truth. He didn't even ask me to take an oath before I testified before his chamber. Is this something you noticed? I didn't draw your attention to that myself, but if you just look at this, if you look at the fact that he didn't ask me to take an oath. All he wanted me to do is to summon all my courage and tell the truth. A witness is in a position that is far worse than that of an accused. I really apologise for having to say this in front of this Trial Chamber, but if given a chance, I could explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you were encouraged by Vesna Krstajic in front of the Belgrade special court --

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was encouraged to tell the truth. I told the truth to the best of my ability, and the naked truth is what I am now sharing with this Chamber and with you. It can be verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I hereby conclude my cross-examination. There is one thing that I wish to say. I must apologise to my learned friend, Mr. Moore, for that remark I made on the transcript. It was in the course of a very strenuous cross-examination. I hope he understands. It won't happen again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Now, Mr. Moore, your re-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I will, if I may. Can I just clarify. I, for my part, would wish the statements of this witness to be placed before the Court as an exhibit. There has been cross-examination on documents, statements that he has made. There has been a large amount of cross-examination. In my submission, it would be an appropriate course if those documents went before the Court, perhaps marked off with a highlighter to demonstrate, as the Defence would say, the inconsistencies. I am in the Court's hands in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore, you well realise that the normal procedure is not to do that, but in this case there has been, as I recall, specific suggestions of recent invention over some material matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And that would justify a departure from the normal course, if it is your contention that the original document read in context would be material to this Chamber's assessment of that proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Yes, I have not applied to do it, as far as I can recollect, with any other witness because there has not been the same, as the Defence would suggest, the same inconsistencies. In our submission, it's an appropriate course for the Court to adopt, and it would go, of course, to the credibility of the witness and the inconsistency, if it be inconsistency, with regard to the context and the totality of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you seek to tender them not for the purpose of establishing the truth of their content but for the purpose of assessing the credibility of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Well, it's that -- not necessarily. In my submission, the normal, from the common-law perspective, is that statements should not go before the Court to demonstrate consistency.
